scenarios.name: single filer, Bailey-vested NC state government pension (stipulated: 5+ years creditable service as of 8/12/1989): fully exempt under the Bailey settlement, engine taxes it in full
scenarios.source: NCDOR 'Bailey Decision Concerning Federal, State and Local Retirement Benefits': 'the North Carolina Consolidated Judicial Retirement System, the Federal Employees' Retirement System, or the United States Civil Service Retirement System, if the retiree had five or more years of creditable service as of August 12, 1989' are exempt from NC income tax; a retiree entitled to the exclusion claims a deduction on 'Line 20, Form D-400, Schedule S 2025 Supplemental Schedule'. This fixture STIPULATES in prose (not in any structured field -- the model has no vesting-date field at all: a household with two government pensions of the identical PlanSource where only one is Bailey-vested cannot be expressed, because both rows decode to the same planSource with no way to distinguish them) that this taxpayer had 5+ years of creditable service in the NC state retirement system as of 8/12/1989, i.e. is Bailey-vested. RE-LABEL DONE, TASK 7 (2026-08-05): this row now reads 'ownStateOrLocal', the case Phase 5b Task 1 added for a taxpayer's OWN state system. It previously read 'otherStateOrLocal', which is definitionally a DIFFERENT state's system and whose whole purpose is to stop an out-of-state pension claiming a state's own exclusion; that was the only available label when this fixture was written, and Task 2 deliberately left North Carolina's re-label to Task 7 so it would land with whatever Task 7 decided about Bailey. The re-label was measured to move no computed value, because North Carolina ships no perSourceExemptions and so reads planSource for nothing. TASK 7 SHIPPED NO BAILEY RULE and this knownDefect block therefore STAYS: the only rule the model can express is keyed on source and structure, and it would exempt every North Carolina state and local pension rather than only the Bailey class, i.e. every NC public employee first hired after August 1984, who cannot have five years of creditable service by 8/12/1989 and is fully taxable. The quoted NCDOR sentence above both GRANTS the exclusion and LIMITS it by that vesting condition in the same clause, so the over-match is excluded by the very sentence that would authorise the rule; that is Hawaii's structure (Task 5), not Massachusetts's (Task 4). See Phase5bNorthCarolinaDecisionTests and the NC entry in GoldenScenarioDefectCatalogueTests.knownButUnpinned. Arithmetic: $50,000 fully excluded, $0 state taxable income after the $12,750 single standard deduction, tax = $0.00.

knownDefect.summary: Bailey-vested NC state/local/federal government pensions are fully exempt from NC tax; statetax-2026-NC.json has no perSourceExemptions (and the model has no vesting-date field to express Bailey status at all -- a household with two government pensions of the identical PlanSource where only one is Bailey-vested cannot be expressed, because both rows decode to the same planSource with no way to distinguish them), so the engine taxes it in full.

scenarios.name: single filer, private-sector pension (never Bailey-eligible): correctly fully taxable, engine also taxes it fully -- contrast/regression case
scenarios.source: NCDOR 'Bailey Decision Concerning Federal, State and Local Retirement Benefits': the exclusion is scoped to specific NC/federal government retirement systems and 'does not apply to retirement benefits paid to former teachers and state employees of OTHER states'; a private-sector employer pension is never a Bailey-covered retirement system regardless of vesting date, so it remains fully taxable under general NC law. Arithmetic: $50,000 - $12,750 single standard deduction = $37,250 taxable x 3.99% flat rate = $1,486.27 (computed as an IEEE-754 double, matching the engine's own arithmetic to the cent).

scenarios.name: MFJ, both spouses Bailey-vested NC state pensions (stipulated): fully exempt, engine taxes the full household income
scenarios.source: NCDOR 'Bailey Decision Concerning Federal, State and Local Retirement Benefits' (see single-filer case above for the exact quote). No dollar cap is stated -- 'All distributions from a qualifying Bailey retirement account...are exempt from state income tax regardless of the source of the funds contained in the account.' This fixture stipulates both spouses are Bailey-vested. RE-LABEL DONE, TASK 7 (2026-08-05): both rows now read 'ownStateOrLocal' for North Carolina's OWN systems; see the single-filer case above for the full record, including why Task 7 shipped no Bailey rule and why this knownDefect block stays. Arithmetic: $40,000 + $35,000 = $75,000, all fully excluded, $0 taxable after the $25,500 MFJ standard deduction, tax = $0.00.

knownDefect.summary: Both spouses' Bailey-vested pensions should be fully excluded; the engine has no perSourceExemptions for NC, taxing the full $75,000 household income.

scenarios.name: MFJ, one spouse's Bailey-vested NC pension is exempt and the other spouse's private pension is not: one spouse qualifies
scenarios.source: NCDOR 'Bailey Decision Concerning Federal, State and Local Retirement Benefits'. RE-LABEL DONE, TASK 7 (2026-08-05): the Bailey-vested row now reads 'ownStateOrLocal' for a North Carolina OWN system; see the single-filer case above for the full record. The private-pension row was correctly labelled and is unchanged. Arithmetic: $40,000 Bailey-vested pension fully excluded; $35,000 private pension fully taxable. $75,000 - $25,500 MFJ standard deduction - $40,000 exclusion = $9,500 taxable x 3.99% = $379.05.

knownDefect.summary: The Bailey-vested spouse's pension should be excluded while the private-pension spouse's income stays taxable; the engine excludes neither (no perSourceExemptions for NC), taxing the full $75,000 -- the identical figure the fully-exempt MFJ case above produces.

scenarios.name: single filer, ANOTHER state's public pension held by an NC resident: never Bailey-covered at any vesting date, correctly fully taxable -- out-of-state guard case
scenarios.source: NCDOR 'Bailey Decision Concerning Federal, State and Local Retirement Benefits': the exclusion 'does not apply to retirement benefits paid to former teachers and state employees of OTHER states'. ADDED BY TASK 7 (2026-08-05) as the guard the single-filer case above called for, and it is the ONLY guard case North Carolina can carry. It is the only one that is VESTING-INDEPENDENT: an out-of-state public pension is fully taxable in North Carolina at every vesting date, so no correct Bailey rule, present or future, can ever make this case exempt, and its expected value asserts nothing the inputs do not carry. A guard case for a NON-Bailey-vested NORTH CAROLINA pension cannot be written, because its inputs would be byte-identical to the single-filer case above (same amount, structure, planSource, age, filing status and AGI) with a contradictory expectedStateTax; that is the blocker recorded in GoldenScenarioDefectCatalogueTests.knownButUnpinned. What this case catches: any future North Carolina perSourceExemptions rule that names 'otherStateOrLocal'. Before Task 7's re-label the three Bailey rows carried that very label, so the natural rule written to make them pass would have named it and handed a full North Carolina exclusion to a California public pension held by an NC resident. That is the Kansas/KPERS trap, and this case is what fails if anyone walks into it. NO knownDefect: the engine is CORRECT here today and must stay correct. Arithmetic: $50,000 - $12,750 single standard deduction = $37,250 taxable x 3.99% flat rate = $1,486.27 (IEEE-754 double, matching the engine's arithmetic to the cent), the same figure the private-sector case above produces from the same income shape.
